01Rationale

Why this level matters

Architecture at scale is decided by what happens between projects: who may choose what, how old systems move, and which vendors you depend on. This level covers governance that helps teams move, and evolution that does not stall, including open-source and sovereign choices.

02Target competencies

Intended learning outcomes

Set guardrails

Write principles and checks that teams follow because they help.

Evolve safely

Plan migrations in steps, with a way back at each step.

Manage dependency

Assess vendor and platform risk, and design the exit before you need it.

Show compliance

Map architecture to risk and compliance needs with evidence you can audit.

03Planned scope

Proposed scope: 12 lessons in 3 modules

This outline describes the intended curriculum. Lesson materials and assessments are not yet available.

Module 1Governance that teams accept

Light rules, automated where possible.

  1. Principles and guardrails
  2. Decision review without a bottleneck
  3. Fitness functions: checks that run automatically
  4. Measuring architectural health

Module 2Evolving systems

Change without stopping the business.

  1. Migration strategies
  2. Technical debt as a list of decisions
  3. Vendor, platform and AI dependency risk
  4. Open source and sovereign options

Module 3Risk and compliance

Evidence an auditor can follow.

  1. Risk registers that get used
  2. Mapping architecture to compliance needs
  3. Auditability and records
  4. Incidents and what they teach

04Planned practical work

Your governance pack

Proposed project: Write the governance pack for a small portfolio of three systems you know. This practical component will be developed and validated before the level opens.

The steps

  1. List the systems and their dependencies
  2. Write five principles with a test for each
  3. Define the review path for a decision
  4. Write one fitness function you can automate
  5. Plan a migration for the riskiest dependency
  6. Write the risk register and compliance map

Intended validation criteria

  • Every principle has a test
  • The migration plan has a rollback at each step
  • Each risk has an owner and a date

05How you learn

Proposed learning design

Worked examples

The professional academies begin with complete examples and make the reasoning behind good decisions visible.

Guided practice

Scaffolds fade as learners progress—from annotated examples to structured tasks and independent work.

Retrieval and review

Low-stakes questions prompt recall; review revisits important concepts. Model answers and rubrics make improvement specific.

Research-informed updates

The academies cite primary research and standards, record review dates and receive versioned updates as evidence changes.

The proposed learning design draws on retrieval practice, worked examples and spaced review; detailed learner materials will be published before release. Read the evidence and sources.

06Intended audience

What it builds on

Level 4, Agentic AI Architecture, or equivalent experience across more than one system.
